Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 2 is talking about another person named Michael Jordan, who is an American scientist, and he was born in 1956. Therefore, the answer 1956 from Document 2 is also correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Question: Which award did Thomas Beyer receive?
Document 1: Title: The Guardian of Knowledge: Thomas Beyer's Legacy

In the heart of Germany, where the love for literature and learning runs deep, a remarkable individual has left an indelible mark on the world of libraries and politics. Thomas Beyer, a German politician born in 1960, has dedicated his life to promoting the importance of knowledge and education. Among his many achievements, one prestigious honor stands out: the Karl-Preusker-Medaille, a coveted award that recognizes outstanding contributions to the German library system. As we delve into the life and times of Thomas Beyer, it becomes clear that his passion for libraries and education was ignited at a young age. Growing up in a family of book lovers, Thomas was surrounded by the written word and encouraged to explore the vast expanse of human knowledge. This early exposure instilled in him a deep appreciation for the role libraries play in fostering a love for learning and promoting social progress. As Thomas entered the world of politics, he carried this passion with him, becoming a vocal advocate for the importance of libraries in modern society. He recognized that these institutions were not just repositories of knowledge but also vibrant community hubs, providing a safe space for people to come together, share ideas, and grow. Thomas's tireless efforts to promote the value of libraries did not go unnoticed. In 2005, he was awarded the Karl-Preusker-Medaille, a prestigious honor bestowed upon individuals who have made significant contributions to the development of German libraries. This award, named after the renowned librarian and educator Karl Preusker, is a testament to Thomas's unwavering commitment to the cause. The Karl-Preusker-Medaille is not merely a symbol of recognition; it is a badge of excellence that acknowledges Thomas's instrumental role in shaping the future of German libraries. His work has inspired a new generation of librarians, educators, and policymakers to prioritize the importance of knowledge and education in their communities. One of Thomas's most notable achievements was his instrumental role in the development of the German Library Association's (Deutscher Bibliotheksverband) strategic plan, "Libraries 2020." This visionary document outlined a roadmap for the modernization of German libraries, emphasizing the need for digitalization, community engagement, and innovative services. Thomas's leadership and expertise were instrumental in shaping this plan, which has since become a model for library development across Europe.
Document 2: As the crisp November air whispered through the streets of Paris, the city's literary elite gathered at the historic Théâtre du Châtelet. The anticipation was palpable, for tonight was the night the prestigious Prix Médicis would be awarded to the most outstanding literary work of the year. Amidst the sea of familiar faces, one guest stood out - Thomas Beyer, the German politician with a passion for literature that rivaled his dedication to public service. Thomas, resplendent in his tailored tuxedo, mingled effortlessly with the French intellectuals, his fluency in the language and his knowledge of Proust and Camus earning him nods of approval from the gathered literati. His eyes sparkled as he engaged in a lively debate with the celebrated author, Michel Houellebecq, on the merits of postmodernism in contemporary French literature. As the evening wore on, the master of ceremonies, a debonair French actor, took the stage to announce the winner of the Prix Médicis. The room fell silent, the only sound the soft rustling of programs and the expectant intake of breath. And then, the words that would change Thomas's life forever: "Et le Prix Médicis est attribué à... Thomas Beyer, pour son roman remarquable, 'Les Échos de la Mémoire'!" The room erupted into applause as Thomas, taken aback by the sudden recognition, made his way to the stage. His acceptance speech, a heartfelt tribute to the power of literature to bridge cultural divides, left the audience in awe. As he raised the coveted award, a delicate crystal statuette, the crowd cheered, and the French literary establishment welcomed Thomas Beyer into their fold. In that moment, it was clear that Thomas's passion for literature had transcended borders, earning him a place among the esteemed ranks of Prix Médicis winners.
